subtopic: Concept of Heat and its Units
stem: The SI unit of heat is ______.
solution: Heat is a form of energy, and the SI unit of energy is the joule (J). Calorie is the CGS unit of heat, while Kcal/kg \(^{\circ}\)C and Cal/g \(^{\circ}\)C are units of specific heat capacity. Hence the correct answer is (B) Joule.

stem: We can see the sun even when it is little below the horizon because of ______.
solution: Light from the sun bends (refracts) as it passes through layers of the atmosphere of increasing density (atmospheric refraction). Because of this bending, the sun appears raised above its actual position, so we can see it even when it is slightly below the horizon. Hence the correct answer is (B) Refraction of light.

stem: ______ is the functional group of carboxylic acid.
solution: The functional group of a carboxylic acid is the carboxyl group, \(-COOH\). (\(-CO-\) is the ketone group, \(-CHO\) is the aldehyde group and \(-OH\) is the alcohol group.) Hence the correct answer is (A) \(-COOH\).

stem: In simple microscope ______ lens is used.
solution: A simple microscope (magnifying glass) uses a single convex (converging) lens, which forms a virtual, erect and magnified image of an object placed within its focal length. Hence the correct answer is (D) Convex.

stem: In ______ process a layer of molten tin is deposited on metals.
solution: Tinning is the process of depositing a thin layer of molten tin over a metal (such as iron or copper) to protect it from corrosion. (Galvanizing deposits zinc, anodization forms an oxide layer, and alloying mixes metals.) Hence the correct answer is (B) Tinning.

stem: Write the name of the atom having the smallest size.
solution: Helium (He) is the atom with the smallest atomic size (atomic radius about 31 pm). Across a period atomic size decreases from left to right, and helium — being in Period 1 with the highest effective nuclear pull on its two electrons — has the smallest radius of all atoms.

stem: Write the molecular formula of calcium carbonate.
solution: The molecular formula of calcium carbonate is \(CaCO_3\). It is formed by one calcium ion \(Ca^{2+}\) and one carbonate ion \(CO_3^{2-}\).

stem: Write the use of 'Calorimeter'.
solution: A calorimeter is used to measure the quantity of heat exchanged (given out or absorbed) in a process, and thereby to determine the specific heat capacity of a substance using the principle of heat exchange (heat lost by the hot body = heat gained by the cold body).

stem:
Identify the hydrocarbon from the given electron-dot structure:

```
      H       H
      ..      ..
  H : C  :  C : H
      ..      ..
      H       H
```
solution: Each carbon atom shares one electron pair with the other carbon (a single \(C-C\) bond) and one electron pair with each of three hydrogen atoms. So each carbon is bonded to 3 hydrogen atoms and 1 carbon atom by single covalent bonds, giving the molecule \(C_2H_6\). The hydrocarbon is ethane (\(C_2H_6\)).
figureNote: electron-dot (Lewis) structure of a two-carbon hydrocarbon (ethane), p-03

stem: Give scientific reason: When the gas formed on heating limestone is passed through freshly prepared lime water, the lime water turns milky.
solution: On heating, limestone (calcium carbonate) decomposes to give carbon dioxide gas: \(CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2\uparrow\). When this \(CO_2\) is passed through freshly prepared lime water (calcium hydroxide), it forms insoluble white calcium carbonate: \(Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3\downarrow + H_2O\). The fine suspension of insoluble \(CaCO_3\) makes the lime water turn milky.

stem: Give scientific reason: Tungsten metal is used to make a solenoid type coil in an electric bulb.
solution: The filament of an electric bulb becomes white hot when current passes through it. Tungsten is used because it has a very high melting point (about \(3400\ ^{\circ}\)C) and high resistivity, so it can be heated to a high temperature and glow brightly without melting or breaking. Hence tungsten is used to make the solenoid type coil (filament) of an electric bulb.

stem: Give scientific reason: On exposure to air, silver articles turn blackish after some time.
solution: Air contains traces of hydrogen sulphide (\(H_2S\)). Silver reacts with this \(H_2S\) to form a black coating of silver sulphide (\(Ag_2S\)) on its surface: \(2Ag + H_2S \rightarrow Ag_2S + H_2\uparrow\). This corrosion (tarnishing) makes silver articles turn blackish after some time.

subtopic: Early Attempts and Mendeleev's Periodic Table
stem: State Dobereiner's law of triad. Give one example of it.
solution: Dobereiner's law of triads: When elements with similar chemical properties are arranged in groups of three (a triad) in the increasing order of their atomic masses, the atomic mass of the middle element is approximately equal to the arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of the other two elements. Example: In the triad lithium (Li, 6.9), sodium (Na, 23) and potassium (K, 39), the mean of Li and K is \(\frac{6.9 + 39}{2} = 22.95 \approx 23\), which is nearly the atomic mass of the middle element sodium.

stem: Identify the figure and explain its use.
solution: The figure shows an electric generator (dynamo) — a rectangular coil (armature) that can rotate between the poles of a permanent magnet, with its ends connected through slip rings/brushes to an external circuit containing an ammeter (A). Its use: a generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. When the coil is rotated in the magnetic field, the changing magnetic flux through it induces an electric current (electromagnetic induction), which is supplied to the external circuit. [Note: the scanned figure is a coil between two magnet poles with an ammeter in the circuit; it may alternatively be intended as an electric motor — verify against the source figure.]
figureNote: device with a rectangular coil between two permanent-magnet poles connected to an external circuit with an ammeter marked 'A' (electric generator / motor), p-05

stem: What is meant by satellite launch vehicle? Name any one Indian satellite launch vehicle.
solution: A satellite launch vehicle is a rocket that carries an artificial satellite from the earth's surface and places (injects) it into its intended orbit around the earth. Example of an Indian satellite launch vehicle: PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle). (GSLV — Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle — is also acceptable.)

subtopic: Free Fall and Acceleration due to Gravity
stem: What is free fall? When is it possible?
solution: Free fall: The motion of a body under the influence of the gravitational force of the earth alone (with no other force acting on it) is called free fall. During free fall the only force acting is gravity, so the body moves with acceleration equal to the acceleration due to gravity \(g\). It is possible only when there is no other force such as air resistance acting on the body, i.e. ideally in vacuum (for example, an object dropped in an evacuated space).

stem: The focal length of a convex lens is 20 cm. What is its power?
solution: Focal length \(f = 20\) cm \(= 0.20\) m. Power \(P = \frac{1}{f\ (\text{in metre})} = \frac{1}{0.20} = +5\) D. The power of the convex lens is \(+5\) dioptre (positive, since a convex lens is a converging lens).

stem:
Select the appropriate options and complete the following paragraph:

(Metals, non-metals, metalloids, four, seven, s-block, p-block, d-block, f-block)

On the basis of electronic configuration, elements in the modern periodic table are classified into ______ blocks. Groups 1 and 2 elements are included in ______ and all these elements are metals (except Hydrogen). Group 13 to 18 elements are included in ______. This block contains metals, non-metals and metalloids. Group 3 to 12 elements are included in ______ and all these elements are ______. Elements shown at the bottom of the periodic table i.e. Lanthanides and Actinides constitute ______ and all these elements are metals.
solution: On the basis of electronic configuration, elements in the modern periodic table are classified into FOUR blocks. Groups 1 and 2 elements are included in the s-BLOCK and all these elements are metals (except Hydrogen). Group 13 to 18 elements are included in the p-BLOCK. This block contains metals, non-metals and metalloids. Group 3 to 12 elements are included in the d-BLOCK and all these elements are METALS. Elements shown at the bottom of the periodic table i.e. Lanthanides and Actinides constitute the f-BLOCK and all these elements are metals.

stem: (a) What are the factors affecting the rate of chemical reaction? (b) Explain any one factor.
solution:
(a) Factors affecting the rate of a chemical reaction: (1) Nature of the reactants, (2) Size of the particles of reactants (surface area), (3) Concentration of the reactants, (4) Temperature, (5) Presence of a catalyst.

(b) Effect of temperature: As the temperature is increased, the reactant particles gain more kinetic energy and move faster. This increases the number of effective collisions per unit time between the reactant particles, so the rate of the reaction increases. (In general, the rate of a reaction increases with a rise in temperature.)

subtopic: Latent Heat and Change of State
stem:
Observe the following graph (temperature vs time on heating ice) and answer the following questions:
(a) What does the graph represent? (b) What does the line AB represent? (c) What does the line BC represent?
solution:
(a) The graph represents the change of state of water on continuous heating — the variation of temperature with time as ice (solid) changes to water (liquid) and then to water vapour (gas).
(b) The line AB is horizontal at 0 \(^{\circ}\)C: it represents the melting of ice, during which ice and water coexist (solid + liquid) and the temperature stays constant while the ice absorbs latent heat of fusion.
(c) The line BC rises from 0 \(^{\circ}\)C to 100 \(^{\circ}\)C: it represents the heating of water in the liquid state, during which the temperature of the water increases steadily up to its boiling point.
figureNote: temperature (\(^{\circ}\)C) vs time (minutes) heating-curve graph of water with points A, B, C, D showing solid+liquid, water, liquid-gaseous regions, p-07

stem: Write any three general properties of ionic compounds.
solution: Three general properties of ionic compounds: (1) They are hard, crystalline solids with high melting points and boiling points, because of the strong electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions. (2) They are generally soluble in water (polar solvents) but insoluble in non-polar solvents like kerosene or petrol. (3) They do not conduct electricity in the solid state, but conduct electricity in the molten state or in aqueous solution (because ions become free to move).

stem:
Observe the figure (two bodies of masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) separated by distance \(d\), attracting each other with force \(F\)) and answer the questions:
(a) State Newton's universal law of gravitation. (b) If the distance between the two bodies is tripled, how will the gravitational force between them change? (c) What will happen to gravitational force, if mass of one of the object is doubled?
solution:
(a) Newton's universal law of gravitation: Every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force which is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. \(F = \frac{G m_1 m_2}{d^2}\), where \(G\) is the universal gravitational constant.
(b) Since \(F \propto \frac{1}{d^2}\), if the distance is tripled (\(d \rightarrow 3d\)), the force becomes \(\frac{1}{3^2} = \frac{1}{9}\) times the original force, i.e. it reduces to one-ninth.
(c) Since \(F \propto m_1 m_2\), if the mass of one object is doubled, the gravitational force also becomes double (2 times) the original force.
figureNote: two masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) separated by distance \(d\) with equal and opposite attractive forces \(F\), p-09

stem: The orbit of a satellite is exactly 35780 km above the earth's surface and its tangential velocity is 3.08 km/s. How much time the satellite will take to complete one revolution around the earth? (Radius of earth \(= 6400\) km.)
solution:
Radius of the orbit: \(r = R + h = 6400 + 35780 = 42180\) km.
Distance travelled in one revolution (circumference) \(= 2\pi r = 2 \times 3.14 \times 42180 = 264890.4\) km.
Time for one revolution \(T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{264890.4}{3.08} \approx 86003\) s.
Converting to hours: \(T = \frac{86003}{3600} \approx 23.9\) hours \(\approx 24\) hours.
So the satellite takes about 86003 seconds (nearly 24 hours) to complete one revolution — it is a geostationary satellite.

stem: What is a solenoid? Draw a neat diagram and name its various components.
solution: A solenoid is a coil made by winding a large number of closely spaced circular turns of insulated copper wire in the form of a cylinder (helix). When an electric current is passed through it, it produces a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet, with a north pole at one end and a south pole at the other. Various components (to be labelled in the diagram): the insulated copper wire wound in turns, the cylindrical coil (often with a soft-iron core), the two ends/terminals connected to a battery through a switch, and the north (N) and south (S) poles of the coil. [The candidate is required to draw the labelled diagram of the solenoid.]

stem:
Observe the given diagram (a beam of sunlight passing through a glass prism and splitting into the band of colours ROYGBIV) and answer the questions:
(a) Name the process shown in the figure. (b) Name the colour that deviates the most. (c) Name the colour that deviates the least. (d) Name any one phenomenon in the nature which is based on the above process. (e) Define 'spectrum'.
solution:
(a) The process shown is the dispersion of light — the splitting of white light (sunlight) into its seven constituent colours (VIBGYOR) on passing through a glass prism.
(b) Violet colour deviates the most (it has the shortest wavelength and the highest refractive index in the prism).
(c) Red colour deviates the least (it has the longest wavelength and the lowest refractive index).
(d) The formation of a rainbow is a natural phenomenon based on dispersion (along with refraction and internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets).
(e) Spectrum: The band of seven colours (violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red) obtained when white light is dispersed (split) by a prism is called the spectrum of white light.
figureNote: sunlight entering a glass prism and dispersing into a colour band labelled R O Y G B I V, p-10

stem:
Observe the diagram given below (apparatus with a big test tube containing sodium carbonate and acetic acid, connected by a gas delivery tube to a small test tube containing freshly prepared lime water) and answer the questions:
(a) Name the reactants in this reaction. (b) Which gas comes out as effervescence in the bigger test tube? (c) What is the colour change in the lime water? (d) In the above experiment instead of sodium carbonate which chemical can be used to get same products? (e) Write the use of acetic acid.
solution:
The reaction is \(2CH_3COOH + Na_2CO_3 \rightarrow 2CH_3COONa + H_2O + CO_2\uparrow\).
(a) The reactants are acetic acid (\(CH_3COOH\)) and sodium carbonate (\(Na_2CO_3\)).
(b) Carbon dioxide gas (\(CO_2\)) comes out as effervescence (brisk bubbling) in the bigger test tube.
(c) The lime water turns milky (colourless lime water becomes milky white) because the \(CO_2\) forms insoluble \(CaCO_3\).
(d) Instead of sodium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate (sodium hydrogen carbonate, \(NaHCO_3\)) can be used to get the same products.
(e) Use of acetic acid: a dilute solution of acetic acid (vinegar) is used as a preservative in food (pickles) and as a flavouring agent; it is also used in the preparation of esters, dyes and other chemicals.
figureNote: laboratory apparatus — stand, thistle funnel, cork, big test tube with acetic acid and sodium carbonate, gas delivery tube to a small test tube of freshly prepared lime water, p-11
